html:
The church of Santa Maria Assunta on the island of Torcello in the northern Venetian lagoon, once the cathedral of the bishops of Torcello and one of the oldest churches in the Veneto. An inscription says it was founded in 639 by Isaac, the Byzantine exarch of Ravenna, when Torcello was still a rival to young Venice. It was rebuilt in 864 and again under Bishop Orso Orseolo, son of Doge Pietro II Orseolo, and consecrated in 1008. The church seen today is mostly this last one: a basilica with a nave and two aisles, a porch in front and a bell tower of the 11th century.

Its mosaics are the earliest that survive around Venice, begun by a team of Byzantine mosaic makers in the late 11th century. In the main apse a tall Virgin holding the Child stands alone on a gold ground above a row of saints. The west wall, done about a century later after an earthquake, is filled from top to bottom by a Crucifixion, Christ breaking open the gates of hell, and a Last Judgment in four bands.

Inside are a marble floor, the throne of the bishops of Altino and the tomb of Saint Heliodorus, first bishop of Altino. The small martyrium church of Santa Fosca stands beside it.
